Package com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest

Class MediaType

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest.MediaType
public final class MediaType extends Object
Pure, dependency-free parser and model for an HTTP media type / Content-Type value as defined by RFC 7231 §3.1.1.1: 

   media-type = type "/" subtype *( OWS ";" OWS parameter )
   parameter  = token "=" ( token / quoted-string )

Both type and subtype are matched case-insensitively and are stored lower-cased. Parameter names are likewise case-insensitive and stored lower-cased, while parameter values are kept verbatim (with any surrounding quotes removed and \ escapes decoded). Insertion order of parameters is preserved so the original ordering can be re-rendered by toString().

The class performs no network or file I/O and is therefore fully offline-testable. Instances are immutable.

  • Method Details

    • parse

      public static MediaType parse(String input)
      Parses a media-type string such as "text/html; charset=UTF-8".

      Surrounding optional whitespace (OWS) is tolerated, as is OWS around the ; parameter separators. Parameter values may be either RFC 7230 tokens or quoted strings; quoted strings are unquoted and their backslash escapes decoded.

      Parameters:
      input - the raw media-type / Content-Type value
      Returns:
      the parsed, immutable MediaType
      Throws:
      MediaType.MediaTypeParseException - if input is null or malformed

    • of

      public static MediaType of(String type, String subtype, Map<String,String> parameters)
      Builds a media type directly from its components without parsing. The type and subtype are lower-cased; parameter names are lower-cased and their iteration order is preserved.
      Throws:
      MediaType.MediaTypeParseException - if the type, subtype or any parameter name is not a valid token

    • matches

      public boolean matches(MediaType pattern)
      Tests whether this concrete media type is matched by pattern, where * in the pattern's type and/or subtype acts as a wildcard. For example application/json matches the patterns application/json, application/* and */*.

      Matching considers only type and subtype; parameters are ignored, which is the common behaviour required for HTTP Accept negotiation.

      Parameters:
      pattern - the (possibly wildcarded) pattern to test against
      Returns:
      true if this media type is covered by pattern

    • toString

      public String toString()
